walkthroughs.body_html:
Italy 1896-1943 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Italy 1896-1943 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Italy 1896-1943.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How did Mussolini become Prime Minister in 1922?
options: Through the March on Rome
By winning a free election
By a military coup against the king
By inheriting the office

mcqs.q: What was the result of the Battle of Adowa in 1896?
options: Ethiopia defeated the Italian army
Italy conquered Ethiopia
Italy gained Libya
A truce with Austria

mcqs.q: Why did Italy feel cheated after the First World War?
options: It received less territory than promised
It lost all its colonies
It was invaded by France
It had stayed neutral
Abyssinia (Ethiopia)
Albania
Greece
Egypt

mcqs.q: Did Mussolini seize power by force in 1922?
options: Mussolini won a landslide free election in 1922.
Italy stayed neutral throughout the First World War.
The March on Rome was a show of strength, but the king legally appointed Mussolini Prime Minister, so it was pressure rather than a violent coup.
Mussolini's Fascists fought their way into Rome and overthrew the king.

mcqs.q: Why did Italy invade Abyssinia in 1935?
options: Abyssinia had invaded Italy first.
Italy invaded Abyssinia to stop a communist takeover.
Mussolini sought empire, prestige and revenge for Adowa in 1896, defying the League of Nations to assert Italian power.
Italy stayed neutral throughout the First World War.

mcqs.q: Was Italy a satisfied victor after the First World War?
options: Italy stayed neutral throughout the First World War.
Despite being on the winning side, Italy gained less than promised, breeding the 'mutilated victory' resentment Fascists exploited.
Mussolini won a landslide free election in 1922.
Italy lost the First World War and was punished like Germany.
